## The challenge

A kNN classifier compares a new image with stored images. This time you will learn parameters that turn pixels directly into ten class scores:

$$S = XW + b.$$

You will convert scores into probabilities, derive the Softmax cross-entropy gradient, verify it with finite differences, and train the classifier using mini-batch stochastic gradient descent.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[Image batch X] --> B[Scores XW + b]
    B --> C[Stable Softmax]
    C --> D[Cross-entropy + L2]
    D --> E[Manual gradients]
    E --> F[SGD update]
    F --> B
```

This is deliberately a manual exercise. The amount of careful calculus and checking needed for one linear layer motivates the computational graphs and backpropagation machinery introduced next.

## What you implement

1. The affine forward pass $XW+b$.
2. Numerically stable Softmax probabilities, after investigating shift invariance.
3. Cross-entropy loss and analytical gradients for $W$ and $b$.
4. One SGD parameter update.

Prediction, mini-batch sampling, epoch training, hyperparameter search, final evaluation, and weight visualization are supplied. Students therefore focus on the mathematical core while still seeing a complete learning system.

## Two-session rhythm

| Session | Work | Checkpoint |
|---|---|---|
| **A · From scores to gradients** | affine scores, max trick, probabilities, cross-entropy, manual derivatives, numerical checking | Checks 1–3 pass |
| **B · From gradients to learning** | SGD update, two-epoch diagnostic, learning-rate/L2 search, final evaluation, learned class templates | Check 4 passes; search and analysis complete |

## Why gradient checking matters

Finite differences provide an independent estimate of a derivative:

$$\frac{\partial L}{\partial w_i}\approx\frac{L(w_i+h)-L(w_i-h)}{2h}.$$

They are far too expensive for training, but extremely useful for detecting an incorrect analytical gradient on a tiny problem. The notebook compares randomly selected entries using relative error.

## Submission standard

Submit the notebook after restarting and running all cells. It must contain:

- four green implementation checks;
- a passing numerical gradient report;
- the two-epoch loss diagnostic;
- the complete validation grid and chosen hyperparameters;
- final train, validation, and test accuracies;
- visualized class weight templates; and
- all reflection prompts answered.
